source_quality.notes: All 25 text pages were extracted. Eight review proxies were inspected. Later formula pages stay on the text layer.

task_reconstruction.summary: Predict 2028 gold and total medals, with an interval, and name who will advance or regress.
Turn a first medal into a binary probability and list countries above 0.2.
Score each sport as its share of a country's medals.
Add a great-coach term and estimate three programs.
Give an original remark on the host effect and on talented athletes.

section_map.summary: Summary of four tasks, then keywords separated by fullwidth semicolons.
Viewers, powerhouses, and the top 10 medalists.
Three assumptions, the second of which concedes that the variables interact.
An ARIMA baseline is written and then left.
A grid-search forest maps athletes, history, events, and host status.
A binary logistic score for countries that have never medaled.
Sport importance as a medal share.
A lasso score with a coaching switch.
Evaluation under the heading Possible Improvements.
Four references, including the Karolyi notice.

contributions.summary: Cross-validation coefficients 0.710 and 0.784 are offered as the check that the forest passed.
Five never-medaled countries are kept because their probabilities exceed 0.2.
A coaching weight of 26.944 is printed, and Romania is printed as rising from 3 to 36.65.

dependency_graph.summary: The ARIMA fits are the reason the forest is introduced.
The sport share I is handed to the coach regression and then shrunk to zero.
The host story returns to the same host indicator the forest already used.

assumptions.summary: 2028 athlete, country, and event counts equal the 2024 counts.
The variables are said to be independent, and the next label says they interact.
The cost of a great coach is excluded, in a fragment labeled Assumption 3.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Order markers and garbled code are named, then cleaned in one short sentence.
Country names are mapped to ISO codes before the files are joined.
USSR and Russia are dropped, with was excluded, and AIN is cleared.

models.summary: ARIMA is displayed as equation (1) and discussed as equation (2).
Two forests, one for gold and one for total, take athletes, history, events, and host status.
A sigmoid and an unsigned loss produce a first-medal probability.
Importance is medals in one sport divided by the country's medals.
A lasso score adds a coaching level that grows and then decays.

verification.summary: Gold cross-validation R2 is 0.710 and total cross-validation R2 is 0.784.
Normality is rejected and a t interval is still reported.
Accuracy 0.841, precision 0.848, F1 0.839, and AUC 0.918 are printed for the logistic fit.
The lasso reports R2 0.708 after importance is dropped.

results_trace.summary: The United States leads both tables. France is second in total. China is second in gold.
LBN, GUM, PLE, ANG, and ESA sit above 0.2.
Chinese women's volleyball goes from 0 to 5.33, Brazilian women's soccer from 6 to 8.86, Romanian gymnastics from 3 to 36.65.

writing_logic.summary: Each summary block opens with For Task and closes the list with Finally and the IOC.
A hypothesis states independence and the justification concedes interaction.
A baseline is praised, measured, and abandoned in one stretch.

language_observations.summary: The opening is an apposition, then not only the athlete but also the country.
there were Great Coach and selected and identify are kept as printed.
Justification: while stays lowercase, and Justification: focuses has no subject.

Table 6 lists eleven total-medal rows under a top-10 caption.

Figure 9 is the residual plot named with the t interval.

Table 9 prints coefficients under the header Waid, and pk has P 0.197.
Figure 12 is the ROC, with AUC 0.918.
Figure 13 is captioned Hybrid Matrix Thermodynamic Diagram.
Table 11 lists five first-medal probabilities, each above 0.2.
Table 13 scores a gold 10, a silver 6, a bronze 3, and no medal 0.

Figure 18 is the lasso path against log lambda, and Figure 19 plots the standardized coefficients.

Figure 20 and Table 15 give the 2028 coached scores, including Romania from 3 to 36.65.

Figure 23 is captioned Sentivity analysis.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge can check whether 0.710 and 0.784 are the cross-validation R2 values rather than correlations.
A judge can test the header Waid and the definition of specificity as FPR against the usual names.
A judge can test whether 3 plus 26.944 accounts for the printed 36.65.

weaknesses.summary: Two training splits are printed for one forest.
The loss called cross-entropy is printed without a minus.
The Romania jump exceeds one step of the coaching coefficient.
The host multiple does not match the 1984 gold labels.

independent_extensions.summary: The interval could be recomputed from the printed t and the printed residual scale, without repairing either.

unresolved_questions: Table 5 on the page 11 proxy shows a row label read as old medals and a repeated GBR. It was not re-cropped.
Table 6 lists eleven countries under a top-10 caption and was not re-cropped.
The page 7 ARIMA table was not opened as a raster, so the orders and the R2 values stay unpaired.
Pages 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, and 24 were not opened as rasters after the eight-proxy cap.
The host prose says 1.4 to 1.9 times. The 1984 gold labels do not sit in that band.
The total interval is printed as plus or minus 15. 1.993 times 7.123 is nearer 14.
Romania's score moves from 3 to 36.65, which is more than one unit of 26.944.
